transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t really stop thinking about my face. Like the left side looks crooked or messed up. I know people say they don’t notice anything, but at work, or even at salsa night, it feels like everyone can see it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to fix how it looks?

Yeah… I do. I check the bathroom mirror a lot before I go back out to the inventory floor. I’ll fix my cap, rub at that same spot on my face… sometimes I get stuck doing it, and then I’m late getting back. My picking numbers fall behind and my boss gets on me about it.
Does this concern about your face cause you a lot of distress or make it hard for you to do things at work, socially, or in other parts of your life?

Yeah… it does. I’ve been written up at the warehouse because I get behind, like I take too long coming back or my work gets delayed.

And I’ve kind of stopped going to stuff… soccer, salsa nights, family gatherings. I just don’t want to deal with people looking at me, or someone taking pictures.
Do you believe that the left side of your face actually looks crooked, or do you think others wouldn’t notice it even if you feel like they do?

I… I think it does look crooked. Like, I know people say they don’t see it, but I can’t really believe that. At the warehouse, or even at salsa night, it feels like everyone notices the left side of my face is messed up.
